title: Oh! Sweet It Is to Know, to Feel
description: Oh! Sweet It Is to Know, to Feel in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 507 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God's Care our Comfort”, where the book credits them to Beard's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Oh! sweet it is to know, to feel, In all our gloom, our wan-derings here, No night of sor-row can con-ceal Man from thy no-tice, from thy care.

lines: Oh! sweet it is to know, to feel,
In all our gloom, our wanderings here,
No night of sorrow can conceal
Man from thy notice, from thy care.
And led through paths of fear and woe,
Say, dost thou love thy children less?
No distance can outreach thine eye,
No night obscure thy endless day:
Be this my comfort when I sigh,
Be this my safeguard when I stray.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
